correctness.rationale: The full height-two incidence algebra has independent cross-edge coordinates. For two idempotents the local product condition is (ur+vs-1)(uy+xs)=0, and a second equation for FE; direct sixteen-state rank verification produces W and W_both uniformly in all finite characteristics. Multinomial vertex-state enumeration yields S and B, while a Hamming-distance defect bound shows each nonground diagonal pattern has weight at most q^(n^2-nd/2), leading to a total O(nq^(-n/2)) relative mass. Conditioning on the two dominant opposite diagonal patterns gives (3+q^(-n^2))/4 and (1+q^(-n^2))/2 exactly. Actual matrix enumeration over F2 and F3 reproduces the predicted counts; finite checks corroborate but do not replace the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The published theory highlights orthodox antichain submonoids, making the frequency of the product-closure property in the nonorthodox full incidence monoid a natural, motivated invariant. The theorem gives exact counts for all bipartite part sizes and every finite field and a sharp universal split: one product idempotent with limiting probability 3/4, both orders with limiting probability 1/2. The persistent one-sided versus two-sided difference is not recoverable from the known component dimensions alone.
